## Description
&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;2K(s) + Cl2(g) → 2KCl(s)&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;Process: Solid potassium metal reacts with chlorine gas. Potassium loses an &#10;&#9;&#9;electron (oxidation) to become K+, and chlorine gains an electron (reduction) &#10;&#9;&#9;to become Cl−. The resulting ions form an ionic lattice.&#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;Stoichiometry:&#10;&#9;&#9;- 2 moles of Potassium, 2×39.10g &#61; 78.20g&#10;&#9;&#9;- 1 mole of Chlorine gas, 1×70.90g &#61; 70.90g&#10;&#9;&#9;Produces 2 moles of Potassium Chloride, 2×74.55g &#61; 149.10g&#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;Energy: The reaction is highly exothermic, releasing significant heat and often producing a &#10;&#9;&#9;characteristic lilac flame (from potassium) and white smoke (KCl particles). &#10;&#9;&#9;
